stucco_surface_input_group.description: Rate per SF applies to net stucco wall field area from PaintScope. Engine divides SF by rate to calculate hours. Texture profile modifier (FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE) is a DUAL multiplier — applies to BOTH labor rates (SF/hr) and material coverage (SF/gal).

task_production_rates.name: Landscape Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy tarps and plastic sheeting along house perimeter where landscape is adjacent. ~30 sec per LF. Includes staking and securing tarps at grade line. LF-based. Identical rate to masonry and siding siblings.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Coverage adequate along working elevation. Minor gaps acceptable if no spray overspray risk.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full perimeter coverage of plantings within spray drift zone (10-15 ft). Secure against wind.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete perimeter coverage secured at all edges. No gaps in protection.

task_production_rates.name: Hardscape Walk Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lay drop cloths and plastic on flat walkway surfaces. ~14 sec per SF. Identical rate to masonry sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Key areas covered. Minor gaps acceptable away from spray zone.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of walkways within overspray zone.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage taped at edges. Non-slip canvas on crew traffic areas.

task_production_rates.name: Hardscape Patio Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lay drop cloths and plastic on flat patio surfaces. ~14 sec per SF. Same rate as walkway protection.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Key areas covered. Minor gaps acceptable away from spray zone.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of patios within overspray zone.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage taped at edges. Non-slip canvas on crew traffic areas.

task_production_rates.name: Light Fixture Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask exterior light fixtures with plastic and stucco tape. ~8.5 min per fixture. Stucco tape required (standard blue tape does not adhere to textured stucco surfaces). Slightly slower than masonry sibling (12 EA/hr) because stucco tape application on textured surface requires more care.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Fixtures covered. Plastic secure.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage with stucco tape sealed at edges. No exposed lens or fixture body.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage sealed at all edges. Stucco tape firmly adhered to textured surface. Double-check seal.

task_production_rates.name: HVAC Unit Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Cover HVAC condenser units with plastic sheeting and secure. ~24 min per unit. Includes securing plastic against wind and ensuring no air intake blockage. Same rate as masonry sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Units covered. Plastic secure.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage secured. Air intake not blocked during non-spray periods.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Secure against wind. Verified no air intake obstruction.

task_production_rates.name: Airless Spray Equipment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Set up airless sprayer, prime pump, install tip (517 for acrylic, 521-525 for elastomeric), install filter (60-mesh for acrylic, 30-mesh for elastomeric), test pattern on cardboard. Stucco-specific: verify tip size for texture profile — deeper textures may benefit from wider fan pattern (619/621). ~35 min per session. Midpoint of 30-45 min range.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Equipment operational. Pattern adequate.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Clean pattern test. Correct tip for material. Pressure verified.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Clean pattern test on cardboard. Correct tip and filter for material type. Pressure set per TDS. Pattern verified for texture profile.

task_production_rates.name: Crack Assessment per Elevation
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walk each elevation and assess all visible cracks. HARD STOP: any crack >1/8 inch requires structural evaluation before proceeding — not a painting scope item. Document crack locations, widths, and patterns. ~45 min per elevation (midpoint of 30-60 min range). Fixed time per elevation — multiply by elevation count at runtime.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Major cracks identified and documented. Structural referral if >1/8 inch.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All cracks mapped. Width measured. Pattern assessed (structural vs shrinkage). Photo documentation.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Comprehensive crack map with measurements. Pattern analysis. Photo documentation. Written referral for any structural concerns.

task_production_rates.name: EIFS Knock Test per Elevation
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Systematically knock-test EIFS surfaces per elevation to detect delamination (hollow sound = EPS separating from base coat). ~45 min per elevation (midpoint of 30-60 min range). Fixed time per elevation. QT3/QT4 only — QT2 spot-check only.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full elevation knock-test. All delamination areas marked. Refer delamination >1 SF for repair.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Systematic grid knock-test at 2 ft intervals. All delamination documented with photos. Written repair referral.

task_production_rates.name: Moisture Testing
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Moisture meter testing of stucco surfaces. Critical for EIFS (moisture behind EIFS causes catastrophic failure). ~45 min per project (midpoint of 30-60 min range). Test at penetrations, below windows, at grade line, and at any discoloration areas.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Spot-check at obvious risk areas (grade, penetrations).
defect_tolerance.QT3: Test at all penetrations, window sills, and grade line. Document readings.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Systematic testing grid. All penetrations, window sills, grade line, and discoloration areas. Written documentation of all readings.

task_production_rates.name: Cure Verification (Traditional Stucco)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Verify new stucco has cured sufficiently for coating. Standard cure: 28 days. Accelerated cure with alkali-resistant primer: 7 days minimum. pH test (phenolphthalein or pH pen). ~20 min (midpoint of 15-30 min range). Administrative verification — not area-dependent.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Cure period confirmed. pH within acceptable range.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Cure period confirmed. pH tested and documented. Alkali-resistant primer confirmed if <28 days.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Cure documentation complete. pH readings at multiple points. Written confirmation of cure status and primer selection rationale.

task_production_rates.name: Pressure Wash (Traditional Stucco)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pressure wash traditional stucco at 1,500-2,500 PSI. Remove dust, efflorescence, loose material. ~7 sec per SF. 24-48 hour dry time before coating. Higher pressure than EIFS wash. Midpoint of 400-600 SF/hr range.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Loose material and dust removed. Surface ready for primer.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Clean surface free of dust, efflorescence, and loose material. Uniform appearance.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Thoroughly clean surface. No residual efflorescence. No loose material. Consistent surface profile.

task_production_rates.name: Low-Pressure Wash (EIFS)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Low-pressure wash EIFS at 400-800 PSI maximum. CRITICAL: high pressure damages EIFS acrylic finish coat and can drive water behind system. ~13 sec per SF. Slower than traditional stucco wash because lower pressure requires more dwell time and passes. Midpoint of 200-350 SF/hr range.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Surface clean. No pressure damage to EIFS finish coat.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Clean surface. No pressure damage. Uniform appearance. Mildew areas retreated.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Thoroughly clean. No pressure damage. Verified no water intrusion at penetrations during wash.

task_production_rates.name: Mildew Eradication Treatment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply bleach solution (1:3 ratio), dwell 15-20 min, scrub with stiff bristle brush, rinse. ~24 sec per SF of affected area. Rate applies to affected area only — not total wall SF. Midpoint of 100-200 SF/hr range.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Visible mildew killed. Surface cleaned.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All mildew eradicated. No live growth remaining. Surface cleaned and rinsed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete eradication verified. Surrounding area treated preventively. Documentation of treatment areas.

task_production_rates.name: Efflorescence Treatment (Traditional Stucco)

QT2.notes: Light dry-brush removal only. No acid treatment.

QT3.notes: TSP wash and brush scrub. Light efflorescence.

QT4.notes: Acid wash (muriatic dilute) for moderate-to-heavy efflorescence. Neutralize, rinse thoroughly.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Efflorescence treatment on traditional stucco. Light treatment (TSP wash + brush): 150-250 SF/hr. Acid treatment (QT4, moderate-heavy): 80-120 SF/hr. Rate applies to affected area only. Traditional stucco only — EIFS does not produce efflorescence.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Loose efflorescence removed. Surface paintable.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Efflorescence removed. Surface clean and dry. No white residue remaining.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete removal. Acid-treated areas neutralized and rinsed. pH verified before priming.

task_production_rates.name: Cosmetic Crack Patching
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fill cosmetic cracks (<1/8 inch) with elastomeric crack sealant. ~48 sec per LF. Cracks >1/8 inch are structural — outside painting scope. Sealant cure time: 24-48 hours before coating. Midpoint of 50-100 LF/hr range. Manual capture LF from field measure.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Visible cracks filled. Sealant flush with surface.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All cosmetic cracks filled. Sealant tooled smooth. Flush with surrounding surface.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All cracks filled and tooled. Sealant blended with surrounding texture. No raised or sunken fill lines.

task_production_rates.name: Surface Patching and Texture Match
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Patch spalled or damaged stucco areas and match surrounding texture profile. ~48 sec per SF of affected area. Texture matching is skill-intensive — dash and lace textures require experienced application. Rate applies to affected area only. Midpoint of 50-100 SF/hr range.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Patches secure and flush. Texture approximation acceptable.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Patches blended with surrounding texture. Good match.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Patches indistinguishable from surrounding texture at 3 ft. Exact texture match.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk Stucco-to-Trim Joints
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply polyurethane caulk to stucco-to-trim transition joints. ~36 sec per LF. Polyurethane caulk preferred for movement joints (Class 25/50). 3-7 day cure before painting. Manual capture LF from field measure. Midpoint of 75-150 LF/hr range.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Joints sealed. Caulk bead continuous.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Clean caulk bead. Tooled smooth. No gaps or voids.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Perfect caulk bead. Tooled smooth with consistent profile. No excess or deficiency.

task_production_rates.name: EIFS Insurance Verification
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Verify CGL insurance covers EIFS work or confirm EIFS-specific rider has been obtained. Administrative gate task — must be confirmed before starting EIFS coating work. ~20 min (midpoint of 15-30 min range). Workflow flag only — does not affect material or labor estimation.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Insurance verified. Written confirmation on file.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Insurance verified. Written confirmation on file. Policy rider documented.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Insurance verified. Written confirmation on file. Policy rider documented. Copy retained in project file.

task_production_rates.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer - Spray + Back-Roll (Traditional Stucco)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray alkali-resistant primer (Loxon or equivalent) then immediately back-roll for penetration and uniformity. 350 SF/hr BASE rate on smooth texture — apply FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE modifier for textured surfaces. Two-person crew (sprayer + roller). Spray/backroll coupling compliant. Critical on traditional stucco — pH up to 13 will destroy standard primer.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Full coverage. No holidays. Primer sealed to surface.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. Back-roll ensures penetration into texture. No bare spots.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage with consistent mil build. Back-roll verified for complete texture penetration. No holidays or thin spots.

task_production_rates.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer - Roll Application (Traditional Stucco)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll alkali-resistant primer with heavy-nap roller (1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch). 200 SF/hr BASE rate on smooth texture — apply FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE modifier for textured surfaces. Single worker. Nap depth must match texture profile for proper penetration.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Full coverage. Primer in all textures.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. Thick nap ensures texture penetration. No bare spots in texture valleys.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage with consistent mil build. Every texture valley primed. No holidays.

task_production_rates.name: Acrylic Primer - Spray + Back-Roll (EIFS)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray 100% acrylic primer on EIFS then back-roll. 400 SF/hr BASE rate — EIFS is smoother than traditional stucco so primer application is faster. Apply FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE modifier if EIFS has textured finish. Two-person crew. Spray/backroll coupling compliant. Vapor-permeable formulation preferred.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Full coverage. Primer uniform.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. Back-roll for adhesion. No bare spots.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage with consistent mil build. Back-roll verified. No holidays.

task_production_rates.name: Acrylic Primer - Roll Application (EIFS)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll 100% acrylic primer on EIFS with appropriate nap roller. 250 SF/hr BASE rate — EIFS smoother surface allows faster roller application than traditional stucco. Apply FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE modifier if EIFS has textured finish. Single worker.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Full coverage. Primer uniform.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. No bare spots. Roller texture consistent.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage. Consistent mil build. No holidays.

task_production_rates.name: Primer - Brush Detail Work
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush primer into detail areas — around penetrations, at trim transitions, in tight corners, and at grade line. 65 SF/hr BASE rate on smooth texture. Apply FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE modifier for textured surfaces. Midpoint of 50-80 SF/hr range. Both primer types.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Primer in all detail areas. No bare spots at transitions.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage in all detail areas. Clean cut lines at trim transitions.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Precise cut lines. No bleed onto adjacent trim.

task_production_rates.name: Acrylic Finish Coat 1 - Spray + Back-Roll
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray acrylic finish then immediately back-roll for uniform texture and mil build. 137 SF/hr BASE rate on smooth texture (midpoint of 125-150 SF/hr). Apply FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE modifier — rougher textures require more passes and material. Two-person crew. Spray/backroll coupling compliant. Lower rate than primer because finish coat requires more precise application for appearance.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. Consistent color. Maintain wet edge.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage and color. Consistent roller texture. No lap marks. No sags or runs.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build. Consistent color and texture. No visible pattern variation. No lap marks, sags, or runs.

task_production_rates.name: Acrylic Finish Coat 1 - Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll acrylic finish with heavy-nap roller. 112 SF/hr BASE rate on smooth texture (midpoint of 100-125 SF/hr). Apply FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE modifier. Single worker. Nap depth matched to texture profile.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. Consistent color.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. No lap marks. Consistent roller texture.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage and mil build. No lap marks. Consistent appearance.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 - Brush Detail Work
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush finish into detail areas — around penetrations, at trim transitions, in tight corners. 45 SF/hr. Both acrylic and elastomeric. Slowest application method — detail work only.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Coverage in all detail areas.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. Clean cut lines. Blended with field application.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Precise cut lines. Seamless blend with field coat. No brush marks visible at 3 ft.

task_production_rates.name: Elastomeric Finish Coat 1 - Spray + Back-Roll
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray elastomeric coating then back-roll for uniform mil build. 90 SF/hr BASE rate on smooth texture (~65% of acrylic spray_backroll rate). Apply FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE modifier. Elastomeric is dramatically heavier body — requires larger tips (521-525), coarser filters (30-mesh), higher pressure (2,300-3,000 PSI). Back-roller must distribute much thicker wet film. Two-person crew. Traditional stucco ONLY — PROHIBITED on EIFS.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Consistent mil build (10-12 mils DFT per coat). No pinholes. Maintain wet edge.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build verified with wet film gauge. No pinholes, sags, or curtaining. Consistent appearance. 10-12 mils DFT per coat.

task_production_rates.name: Elastomeric Finish Coat 1 - Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll elastomeric coating with heavy-nap roller. 75 SF/hr BASE rate on smooth texture (~65% of acrylic roll rate). Apply FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE modifier. Elastomeric is very heavy body — roller loads slowly, requires firm pressure to distribute. Single worker. Traditional stucco ONLY.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Consistent thickness. No pinholes.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build. No pinholes or thin spots. Wet film gauge verification.

task_production_rates.name: Acrylic Finish Coat 2 - Spray + Back-Roll
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 spray_backroll. Sealed surface provides consistent absorption. Two-person crew. Final appearance coat.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage and color. No visible pattern at 6 ft. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. Final appearance coat. Consistent sheen.

task_production_rates.name: Acrylic Finish Coat 2 - Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 roll. Sealed surface. Final coat.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. Consistent roller texture. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage and mil build. No lap marks. Final coat.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 - Brush Detail Work
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 brush detail. Final coat detail work.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. Clean cut lines. Blended with field coat. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Precise cut lines. Seamless blend. No brush marks at 3 ft. Final coat.

task_production_rates.name: Elastomeric Finish Coat 2 - Spray + Back-Roll
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 elastomeric spray_backroll. First coat provides sealed surface. Final coat — verify cumulative DFT target (20-30 mils). Traditional stucco ONLY.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Cumulative DFT target 20-24 mils. No pinholes. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build. Cumulative DFT 24-30 mils verified with wet film gauge. No defects. Final coat.

task_production_rates.name: Elastomeric Finish Coat 2 - Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 elastomeric roll. Sealed surface. Final coat — verify cumulative DFT. Traditional stucco ONLY.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Cumulative DFT on target. No pinholes. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build verified. Cumulative DFT 24-30 mils. Final coat.

task_production_rates.name: Interstage Inspection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walk all elevations after first finish coat. Check for holidays, thin spots, lap marks, sags. Note areas for touch-up before second coat. ~25 min per session (midpoint of 20-30 min range). QT3 visual scan; QT4 systematic with raking light.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Visual scan of all elevations. Major defects noted.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Systematic inspection with raking light. All defects documented. Photo documentation of areas requiring touch-up.

task_production_rates.name: Interstage Light Sand (QT4 Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 220 grit light sand on anomalies only — do NOT attempt to sand entire textured stucco surface. ~14 sec per SF. Address nibs, runs, sags, and surface irregularities identified during interstage inspection. QT4 only. Midpoint of 200-300 SF/hr range.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Anomalies sanded smooth. No deep scratches. Dust removed. Surface ready for coat 2.

task_production_rates.name: Interstage Dust Removal (QT4 Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth or vacuum dust removal after interstage sanding. ~7 sec per SF. Must be thorough — sanding dust trapped under coat 2 creates nibs. QT4 only. Midpoint of 400-600 SF/hr range.

defect_tolerance.QT4: All sanding dust removed. Surface clean and dry. Ready for coat 2.

task_production_rates.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection

QT2.notes: Ground-level walkthrough. Quick scan for obvious misses.

QT3.notes: Ground-level walkthrough at 6-10 ft viewing distance. Backlight check (late afternoon sun angle) on primary elevation.

QT4.notes: Ground-level with binoculars for upper elevations. Raking light and backlight check on all elevations. For elastomeric: verify DFT documentation.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Final walkthrough of all elevations. Stucco-specific: check texture consistency, coverage uniformity, and crack patch blending. For elastomeric: verify cumulative DFT documentation. Range 30-60 min by tier.

defect_tolerance.QT2: No obvious misses or holidays visible from ground.
defect_tolerance.QT3: No defects visible at 6-10 ft from ground level. Backlight passes.
defect_tolerance.QT4: No defects visible at 6 ft with binoculars. Coverage uniform across all elevations. DFT verified for elastomeric.

task_production_rates.name: Final Touch-Up

QT2.notes: Minimal touch-up. Fix obvious misses only.

QT3.notes: Fix all noted defects. Focus on holidays and crack patch areas.

QT4.notes: Fix every defect. Blend seamlessly. Focus on texture consistency and coverage uniformity.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. Rate is per affected area SF — most total wall area passes without touch-up. Stucco touch-up is slower than siding due to texture matching requirement.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Obvious misses touched up.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All noted defects repaired. Crack patches blended.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects repaired. Touch-ups blended seamlessly with surrounding texture and color.

task_production_rates.name: Protection Material Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all stucco tape, landscape tarps, hardscape covers, fixture bags, HVAC covers, and plastic sheeting. ~30 min per session (midpoint of 20-40 min range). Check for stucco tape adhesive residue — stucco tape can leave residue if overexposed to UV on multi-day projects. Verify no paint on protected surfaces.

defect_tolerance.QT2: All protection materials removed.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All materials removed. No tape residue on surfaces. Check landscape for overspray.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All materials removed. Tape residue checked and cleaned. All protected surfaces inspected for paint contamination.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Equipment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Flush airless sprayer (full flush cycle). Clean tips and filters. Inspect tips for wear. Clean roller frames, dispose of saturated thick-nap covers. ~25 min per session (midpoint of 20-30 min range). Elastomeric coatings require more thorough flushing due to heavy body — add 10 min for elastomeric projects.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Equipment flushed and stored.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full flush. Tips and filters cleaned. Tip wear inspected. Roller covers disposed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full flush cycle. Tips and filters cleaned and inspected. Equipment ready for next use.

task_production_rates.name: Waste Disposal and Site Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Collect all debris — caulk tubes, stucco tape, plastic sheeting, paint cans, used roller covers, spray tips, filters. Dispose properly. Final site walkthrough. ~20 min (midpoint of 15-30 min range).

defect_tolerance.QT2: All debris collected and disposed.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Site restored to pre-work condition. All materials removed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Site restored. Walkthrough with customer. No evidence of work activity.

factor_modifiers.name: Stucco Texture Profile DUAL Modifier (Labor + Material)
factor_modifiers.description: DUAL modifier — applies to BOTH labor production rates (SF/hr) AND material coverage rates (SF/gal). Rougher textures slow production AND increase material consumption. This is the dominant cost driver for stucco work.
factor_modifiers.notes: Smooth is baseline (1.00x). Sand adds 25% time and 25% material. Lace adds 50% time and 50% material. Dash/roughcast doubles both time and material — deep texture valleys require heavy loading and multiple passes. This is the PRIMARY cost driver for stucco projects. Stacks with FAC_STCO_SUBSTRATE_TYPE and FAC_EXT_ACCESS.

factor_modifiers.name: Stucco Substrate Type Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Substrate type affects production rate. EIFS is smoother and less porous than traditional stucco — slightly faster application. Labor rate modifier ONLY — does not affect material coverage (material coverage is driven by texture_profile and coating_system).
factor_modifiers.notes: Traditional stucco is baseline (1.00x). EIFS is 10% faster (0.90x modifier = effective_rate = base / 0.90, so rate increases ~11%). EIFS has smoother surface, lower porosity, more consistent absorption. Labor rate modifier ONLY — material consumption is NOT affected by substrate type (driven by texture_profile instead). Note: EIFS primer and traditional primer tasks are already separate (different products), so this modifier primarily affects the shared finish tasks.

factor_modifiers.name: Access Type Height Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Access type drives production rate reduction for elevated work. Applied per elevation. Ground tasks (equipment setup, protection, site cleanup) are not affected.
factor_modifiers.notes: Applied per elevation. Protection setup/teardown, spray equipment setup, cure verification, EIFS insurance verification, moisture testing, crack assessment, EIFS knock test, tool cleaning, and waste disposal are ground-level or administrative tasks — not affected.

factor_modifiers.name: Quality Tier Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Quality tier affects overall production pace for tasks that are not already qt_scaled. QT2 is faster (economy pace), QT4 is slower (premium scrutiny). Applied to binary tasks only — qt_scaled and qt_conditional tasks already have tier-specific rates.
factor_modifiers.notes: QT2 is 15% faster (economy pace, less scrutiny). QT3 is baseline. QT4 is 20% slower (premium scrutiny, careful application). Applied to binary tasks only — qt_scaled and qt_conditional tasks already encode tier differences. Protection tasks at QT2 can be slightly less thorough = faster.

factor_modifiers.name: Wind Condition Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Wind affects spray operations (overspray drift, pattern disruption) and general exterior work pace. High wind blocks spray entirely (SOP exclude_when). Moderate wind slows spray work.
factor_modifiers.notes: High wind BLOCKS spray operations per SOP site_condition_rules. Moderate wind (5-10 mph) slows spray 15% due to pattern disruption and repositioning. Roll and brush operations are not significantly affected by wind — modifier applies to spray tasks only.

factor_modifiers.name: Sun Exposure Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Full sun exposure on stucco surfaces can cause flash drying of coatings. Forces early morning start and may reduce daily working hours. Stucco retains heat — surface temp can exceed air temp.
factor_modifiers.notes: Full sun on stucco causes rapid surface heating. Flash drying causes lap marks, poor leveling, and reduced film build. Especially critical for elastomeric coatings — heavy body dries faster in heat. Modifier reflects slower pace to maintain wet edge and may force elevation sequencing.

factor_modifiers.name: Surface Temperature Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Extreme surface temperatures affect coating application. Cold surfaces (<50F) extend recoat intervals. Hot surfaces (>90F) cause flash drying.
factor_modifiers.notes: Optimal: 50-90F surface temp. Cold surface (<50F): coatings cure slower, recoat windows extend, productivity drops 10%. Hot surface (>90F): BLOCKED per SOP — coating fails to level before skinning. Stucco and masonry retain heat longer than wood — surface temp can exceed air temp significantly.

quality_effects.notes: Economy tier. Single finish coat of acrylic on primed surface. No interstage module (single coat). Elastomeric NOT available at QT2 (application complexity exceeds economy scope). Both substrate types require primer (alkali-resistant for traditional, acrylic for EIFS).
Standard tier. Two finish coats (acrylic or elastomeric). Interstage inspection and touch-up between coats. No interstage sanding. Both coating systems and substrate types available.

Premium tier. Two finish coats with premium products. Interstage sand on anomalies (QT4 only). Interstage dust removal. Systematic raking light and backlight inspection. Both coating systems and substrate types available.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Smooth traditional stucco, acrylic, ground access, QT3 baseline (spray_backroll)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Best case — fastest finish production per 2-person crew-hour on traditional stucco.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Smooth EIFS, acrylic, ground access, QT3 (spray_backroll)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: EIFS substrate is 10% faster. 137 / 0.90 = 152 SF/hr. EIFS smoother surface allows faster application.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Sand texture, traditional stucco, acrylic, ground, QT3 (spray_backroll)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Sand texture reduces effective rate by 25%. 137 / 1.25 = 110 SF/hr.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Lace texture, traditional stucco, elastomeric, scaffold, QT4 (spray_backroll)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Heavy modifier stack: lace texture + scaffold + QT4 on elastomeric base rate. 90 / 2.88 = 31 SF/hr per 2-person crew. Slow but viable.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Dash texture, traditional stucco, elastomeric, scaffold, QT4 — WORST CASE (spray_backroll)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Near 4.0x stacking cap (3.84x). 90 / 3.84 = 23 SF/hr per 2-person crew. Extremely slow — flag for estimator review. Dash texture + elastomeric + scaffold + QT4 is the most labor-intensive combination.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Dash texture, traditional stucco, acrylic, scaffold, QT4 — worst case acrylic (spray_backroll)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Near 4.0x stacking cap (3.84x). 137 / 3.84 = 36 SF/hr. Acrylic worst case is still faster than elastomeric worst case due to higher base rate.

assumptions: Base rates for spray_backroll are per crew-hour with 2 workers (sprayer + roller). crew_size = 2.
Base rates for roll and brush are per single worker. crew_size = 1.
Spray/backroll coupling rule satisfied on all spray_backroll tasks: spray component rate <= backroll component rate (same combined rate).
FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE is a DUAL modifier — applied to BOTH labor rates (SF/hr) and material coverage (SF/gal). This is unique to stucco — most modifiers are labor-only.
FAC_STCO_SUBSTRATE_TYPE applies to LABOR rate only — NOT material coverage. Material consumption is driven by texture_profile and coating_system.

Elastomeric base rates (~65% of acrylic) already account for heavier body material — no separate coating_system modifier needed (unlike masonry which uses FAC_MSRY_COATING_SYSTEM). Stucco spec uses separate task IDs for acrylic vs elastomeric finish instead.
Modifier stacking is multiplicative: effective_rate = base_rate / (texture_profile x substrate_type x access x QT).
Maximum combined modifier: 3.84x (dash 2.00 x traditional 1.00 x scaffold 1.60 x QT4 1.20). Under 4.0x stacking cap.
EIFS modifier (0.90) is a rate INCREASE — effective_rate = base / 0.90 makes application faster. This is correct per division formula.
Cure verification is FIXED time — not area-dependent. Administrative verification task.
Crack assessment and EIFS knock test are FIXED per elevation — multiply by elevation count at runtime.
Mildew treatment and efflorescence treatment rates apply to AFFECTED AREA only — not total wall SF.
Environmental conditions (wind, sun, surface temp) are declared as modifiers per exterior doctrine. High wind and hot surface BLOCK spray operations.
EIFS insurance verification is a workflow gate — does not affect labor or material estimation.
No block filler module (unlike masonry CMU) — stucco has continuous surface without block voids.
Stucco tape required for all masking on textured stucco — standard blue tape does not adhere. This affects fixture masking rate (slower than masonry).
risks: Dash texture + elastomeric + scaffold + QT4 is near 4.0x stacking cap (3.84x) — flag for estimator review on these combinations.

DUAL texture modifier on material coverage is critical for accurate material quantity estimates — dash texture uses 2x material vs smooth. Under-estimation on dash/lace textures is a significant cost risk.

Elastomeric on textured stucco is extremely material-intensive — 100-175 SF/gal on smooth baseline DIVIDED by texture modifier. Dash + elastomeric = ~50-87 SF/gal. Material cost alone can exceed $3/SF.
EIFS knock test may reveal delamination requiring repair — outside painting scope but blocks coating work. Project scheduling risk.
Moisture behind EIFS is catastrophic — coating over moisture-compromised EIFS leads to blistering, peeling, and potential structural damage. Moisture testing is a critical gate task.
Crack width >1/8 inch is a HARD STOP — structural evaluation required. This can halt projects if structural repair is needed before coating.
Stucco tape adhesive residue can occur if tape is left on for extended UV exposure — flag for multi-day exterior projects.
Cure verification on traditional stucco — if stucco is <7 days old, alkali-resistant primer may not be sufficient. Full 28-day cure is safest.
Efflorescence on traditional stucco can recur after treatment — may require retreatment if efflorescence reappears before priming.
Touch-up rates are lower than masonry sibling because stucco texture matching is more difficult — touch-ups on textured stucco are visible if not blended properly.
validation_plan: Time 3 acrylic spray_backroll finish projects on smooth traditional stucco at ground access to calibrate baseline 137 SF/hr per 2-person crew.
Time 2 elastomeric spray_backroll projects on smooth traditional stucco to validate 90 SF/hr baseline.
Compare smooth vs sand vs lace texture production rates on same project to validate texture_profile modifier values (1.00/1.25/1.50).
Time 1 dash texture project to validate 2.00x texture modifier — most extreme texture multiplier.
Compare EIFS vs traditional stucco production rates on similar-texture projects to validate 0.90x substrate_type modifier.
Track material consumption per SF by texture profile to validate dual texture modifier on coverage rates.
Time 2 roll-only finish projects on stucco to validate 112 SF/hr acrylic baseline.
Track pressure wash rates: traditional stucco (1,500-2,500 PSI) vs EIFS low-pressure (400-800 PSI) to validate 500 vs 275 SF/hr.
Track crack assessment time per elevation to calibrate 45 min/elevation baseline.
Track EIFS knock test time per elevation to calibrate 45 min/elevation baseline.
Compare equipment cleanup time: acrylic-only projects vs elastomeric projects to validate 25 min vs 35 min baseline.
Track mildew treatment time per SF of affected area to validate 150 SF/hr baseline.
